thread:
priya_cs: Acme (onboard) reports short burst of 429s at SDK init when using Fastly edge with HTTP/3 enabled. Happens only during rapid scale-ups.
eli_support: Can you share sdk version and a sample request_id? Also browser or server SDK?
priya_cs: sdk=0.11.2-server; request_id=rid_f12ab9; sample log: `2026-04-05T14:02:10Z rid_f12ab9 PRECHECK 429 retry-after:1s proto=h3 fastly`
acme-sre: We're spawning 40 short-lived containers (k8s pods) on deploy. Each pod does SDK.init() in prestart hook. Token TTL nominally 12s but our clock sync is off ~3s.
dan_backend: Likely two things: (1) init stampede + low TTL -> many overlapping preflight checks; (2) some HTTP/3 edges split connections per pod causing per-conn rate keys to blow up.
jen_devx: Quick mitigation: set staggered init envs and reduce parallelism. Use these envs: `REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_PARALLEL=3` and `REDWOOD_SDK_INIT_STAGGER_MS=250`. Also add small token-grace: `REDWOOD_TOKEN_REFRESH_MARGIN_MS=500`.
priya_cs: Sending the snippet to Acme now. Repro steps in their staging: roll 50 pods quickly and tail `preflight` metric.
acme-sre: Tested: with stagger+parallel=3 we cut 429s in first 30s by ~85%. With HTTP/3 disabled at Fastly it drops to near zero.
eli_support: Good signal. Follow-ups: (A) DevEx: add onboarding note about HTTP/3 edges and init-stagger; (B) Runtime: consider using client-id header as primary rate key and tolerate truncated XFF; (C) CS: schedule 20min sitdown with customer to confirm renewal health.
jen_devx: I'll draft the blurb and add a short runbook to the onboarding checklist.
dan_backend: Opening RUN-4992 to investigate rate-key resilience (will attach logs).
infra-bot: monitor: canary/acme preflight-429 rate sampled -> 10s windows: peak=92 events, alert threshold=70.
priya_cs: Thanks team — setting follow-up with Acme for 09:30 UTC tomorrow. We'll revert HTTP/3 once runtime fix lands.
